Review: streak-freeze PR #38

2 findings

11 Jul 2026 · reviewed by Claude · pulse-api, branch feat/streak-freeze

Summary

The endpoint works for the happy path, but the streak update is not atomic — two concurrent check-ins can consume one freeze twice. One data-integrity fix is required before merge; the validation gap is minor.

Findings

FindingWhereSeverity
Read-modify-write race on streak freeze consumption store/streaks.ts:114 high
days param accepted unvalidated (negative values roll streaks back) routes/freeze.ts:27 low

Race on freeze consumption

The handler reads freezesRemaining, decrements it in memory, then writes it back. Two check-ins for the same member arriving in the same window both read 1, both write 0, and the member gets two frozen days for one freeze. The client retries on timeout, so this happens in practice, not just in theory.

Risk: concurrent check-ins double-spend a streak freeze, silently corrupting streak history.

Fix: make the decrement conditional in the store — UPDATE … SET freezes = freezes − 1 WHERE freezes > 0 — and branch on the affected-row count.

Unvalidated days parameter

The route parses days with Number() and passes it straight to the store. days=-3 subtracts from the streak; days=1e9 allocates a huge date range. Clamp to the product limit (1–7) and reject non-integers.

Note: auth and rate-limiting on the new route follow the existing middleware chain correctly — nothing to change there.
